//: Which parts of docker-compose.yml are load-bearing for a workbench.
This is a PARTIAL description, not a whitelist. Services it does not name
are not the workbench's business: add Redis, a worker, a virus scanner, a
second frontend, or anything else your app needs, and nothing here
objects. `terp verify --only workbench` checks only whether what this file
CLAIMS is still true -- that a declared role points at a service that
exists, and that a service declaring a host-port variable actually uses
it. A fixed host port is the one thing that really breaks: two projects
cannot then run at once.
Development only. This never describes docker-compose.prod.yml -- how you
deploy is yours to decide.
If your inner loop is not Compose at all -- Tilt, a devcontainer, a
Makefile, bare processes -- add a "commands" block naming how to start,
stop and observe it, and a workbench drives it instead of assuming
Compose. Slots you leave out are NOT filled in from the Compose
defaults: a repair we never saw you declare is a destructive command
nobody asked for. Only the shape of those commands is checked.
If your development loop does not fit this shape at all, replace the whole
file with {"unmanaged": true, "reason": "why"}. The check then stops, and
a workbench falls back to its configured commands and says plainly that it
cannot determine your app's status.
The template seeds this file once and never overwrites it (copier
_skip_if_exists), so a topology you change stays changed across upgrades.
